text:
lina: Quick heads up from onboarding run for Hound-70B quant candidate (v0.2). Found a reproducible KV-cache divergence tied to hot-reloads + tiny RoPE rescale. Sharing repro and ideas.

lina: Repro summary: run a long prefill (80k tokens), then trigger a rolling restart on the same node. After restart we see a cluster of prefix misses and 1-2 token-level divergences downstream. Cold start/no-reload runs are clean.

ark: can you paste the exact commands you used?

lina: minimal repro (canary pool):
```bash
# prefilling long context and recording kvcache fingerprints
redwoodctl api call --model hound-70b:v0.2 --prompt long_story.txt --seq 81920 --trace kvcache > /tmp/hound_trace.log
# trigger rolling restart on the node handling the session
redwoodctl node restart --node-id gpu-canary-21 --grace 30s
```

lina: log fragment: 
```
[2026-02-02T09:12:10Z] prefill complete tokens=81920 fingerprint=0x9d4f22 shard=2 rot_scale=1.0005
[2026-02-02T09:12:42Z] rolling-restart: node gpu-canary-21 draining
[2026-02-02T09:12:52Z] kvcache: fingerprint-check shard=2 old=0x9d4f22 new=0x3a7b9e -> miss
[2026-02-02T09:12:52Z] generation: diverged token_at=81805 expected="and" got="an"
```

mike: Hmm same pattern we saw before but different model. Any quantization changes applied?

lina: This run used int4-A (non-linear scale) config for latency reasons. I also tried an int8 baseline and the problem persisted (smaller incidence). The common factor is the node reused GPU memory; if we force a full process restart (cold), no mismatch.

zara: Could be non-deterministic math / FP to int conversion inside fingerprint. Are we mixing fp32 rot_scale with an FP->hash path?

lina: yes fingerprint algo: hash(layer_idx ^ round(rot_scale * 1e6) ^ shard_seed). We convert rot_scale to u32 via f32 bits on the hot path to be fast.

ark: that conversion is brittle across kernel changes. Some of the new CUDA kernels we've selected do fused multiply-add in different order and can flip low bits. If the fingerprint feeds cache key directly, minute FP diffs become cache misses. We should stop using raw float bits.

lina: short-term mitigation I pushed: if rollout controller detects binary-hash change OR rot_scale delta > 1e-6 then set rollout.meta.kvcache_flush=true. PR: https://redwood.internal/r/redwood/rollout/+/3653

mike: long-term fix ideas:
- canonicalize rot_scale as fixed-point (int64) before hashing
- add a fingerprint-epoch header that increments whenever runtime kernel/quant policy changes
- treat kvcache keys as (model_version, fingerprint_epoch, fingerprint) so reloads with different epochs never attempt reuse

zara: I like epoch header. Also add a debug flag to capture pre/post fingerprints per-session automatically when rollout active, to build a small diffs table.

deploy-bot: Rolling restart initiated for gpu-canary-21 (id: rr-20260202-21). kvcache_flush=false by default.

lina: I'll run a micro sweep overnight: 5k prefills x 3 quant configs (int8, int4-A, int3) with and without forced process restarts, capture mismatch rate and per-shard fingerprint deltas. Will post CSV and artifact link here.

ark: I'll add an integration test that simulates hot-reload on reused memory and asserts 0.5% max token divergence for 64k+ sequences. If test fails, block rollouts in CI.

mike: also recommend we add a small probabilistic kvcache-consistency check in runtime: sample a prefix fingerprint and do an in-memory compare of first/last kv rows after a reload; if mismatch, trigger auto-flush and emit metric kvcache.autoflush.triggered. Could avoid user-visible regressions.

lina: good plan. Filing ticket ONB-442 with repro artifacts and proposed patches. I'll attach trace logs and a short bisect script.

zara: thanks. assign to runtime+infra+quant and ping me on slack when results posted. :sparkles:

deploy-bot: Rolling restart completed for gpu-canary-21. Monitoring kvcache.miss_rate and generation.divergence.*

lina: will update with overnight sweep results in the morning.
